intended_object: The canonical isomorphism H^i(K[n]) ≅ H^{i+n}(K) between the cohomology of a shifted ℤ-indexed cochain complex and the cohomology of the original complex. This is inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The body evaluates Mathlib's natural isomorphism `CochainComplex.ShiftSequence.shiftIso C n i (i + n) _` at `K`. That natural isomorphism is `shiftFunctor n ⋙ homologyFunctor i ≅ homologyFunctor (i+n)`. The side condition `n + i = i + n` is closed by `omega`. Evaluated at `K`, this gives exactly `(K⟦n⟧).homology i ≅ K.homology (i + n)`, which is the standard identification of the cohomology of a shifted complex. With Mathlib's convention `(K⟦n⟧)^p = K^{p+n}`, the target degree `i + n` is correct.

The definition is a thin wrapper that specializes Mathlib's construction to an object. It does not re-implement anything.

The ambient `[Abelian C]` hypothesis is stronger than Mathlib needs, since `shiftIso` only requires a preadditive category with homology. This is the setting of the library's additive Euler characteristic development, and the wrapper adds no mathematical content of its own. So the extra hypothesis is not a meaningful narrowing.
